transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Markus Lee (Echelon ML Eng); Rita Gomez (Echelon Head of Platform); Tom Alvarez (CTO)

Summary: Quick weekly POC check-in focused on INT8 vs FP8 signal: performance deltas, quality regression triage, and runbook for next precision sweep. Agreed to a small experiment: rerun INT8 baseline with changed batching and capture p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput; gather labeled 500-query set for quality A/B.

Topics: KPIs (latency, throughput, SNR for classification tasks), quantization sensitivity, operator rollback plan, KV cache behavior, routing/fallback to hosted variant, pilot SOW & pricing.

Notes/Links: Bench spreadsheet: [pilot-results-spreadsheet] (uploaded by Priya). Security pack & SOW draft: [redwood-pilot-sow.pdf].

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep to 60 mins. Quick roll call, then Priya will walk through the new throughput table we dropped in earlier this morning.
[00:12] Markus Lee: Yep, Markus here. excited to see the numbers — we ran some internal runs overnight.
[00:20] Rita Gomez: Rita on my side. Two folks on infra are listening in case we need to do network stuff.
[00:26] Tom Alvarez: Tom here, will step in if we want to discuss capex/contract.
[00:32] Priya Shah: Cool, thanks. So agenda: 1) perf delta summary int8 vs fp8, 2) quality regression examples, 3) quick tuning experiment idea + runbook, 4) next steps.
[01:03] Priya Shah: Alright slide one — throughput deltas, note we measured on the Aurora-40 instances (roughly what we provisioned in the pilot). INT8 gives ~1.9x tokens/sec vs FP16 baseline, FP8 sits about 1.7x but with slightly lower memory pressure. There is noise so see the sheet for p50/p95.
[01:42] Markus Lee: When you say p95 noise — is that network or model variance?
[01:51] Priya Shah: Mostly model-side kv cache warming and attention recompute on long sequences — the network a bit but we throttled it. There's a mix. The KV cache hit rate was lower on some prompt patterns.
[02:18] Jordan Kim: Quick note — kv cache was transcribed as "K V cash" in earlier notes, ha.
[02:26] Rita Gomez: ha yeah. Also, we noticed spikes on low-length prompts, which surprised us.
[02:33] Priya Shah: That's the batching boundary effect; with batch size 1 you'll see a different p95 tail. Our proposal: rerun INT8 baseline with batch=2 and with batch=4 to see batch sensitivity and latency percentiles.
[03:10] Markus Lee: Why not batch=8? Our traffic is fairly bursty and a lot of calls are short.
[03:19] Priya Shah: batch=8 will move the latency baseline up; we want to keep tail latency under your 200ms p95 SLO. If your traffic pattern is mostly short, batch=2 is a practical sweet spot. But we can run a sweep.
[03:45] Tom Alvarez: cost delta — what are we looking at? Rough factor?
[03:50] Priya Shah: Roughly INT8 reduces raw compute ops and GPU RAM, so cost per token about 0.6x vs FP16. FP8 is similar but slightly less stable for some seeds; so pricing tier might be 0.65x. We'll put concrete numbers in the pricing spreadsheet.
[04:12] Jordan Kim: Ok we'll include that in the revised pilot pricing.
[04:25] Priya Shah: Now quality — we ran the sensitivity sweep on the 1k dev set you provided last week. Overall accuracy drop on classification tasks for INT8 was 0.8% absolute, FP8 about 1.3% on average, but distribution matters: for certain long-context prompts FP8 had 2.7% drop.
[04:58] Markus Lee: Hmm 2.7% on long-context is a bit high — can you show an example?
[05:05] Priya Shah: Yes — example prompt where the model needs to reconcile earlier chat history — FP8 sometimes repeats or hallucinates a prior entity. I'll read a snippet: "...and then the patient reported no prior cardio —" in FP8 we saw occasional insertion of unrelated med names.
[05:39] Rita Gomez: that's worrying for us; our compliance team will flag hallucination risk.
[05:47] Priya Shah: understood — that's why the runbook includes fallback routing: if we detect low-confidence (we can use log-prob delta or Redwood's scoring hook), route to FP16-hosted variant for that request.
[06:10] Markus Lee: How quick is fallback? Latency hit?
[06:16] Priya Shah: On a routed request it's essentially a cold fallback — latency will be higher, maybe add 120-200ms depending on region. We're exploring async re-score patterns to hide that.
[06:34] Jordan Kim: Also, if you want to smooth rollout we'll do canary at 5% then 25% then 100% with automatic rollback trigger on quality thresholds.
[06:47] Tom Alvarez: Are those triggers integrated with our SLOs? We don't want silent degradation.
[06:53] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood Console can tie the eval set (the 500 queries we asked for) to alerts — a 1% drop on the dev set triggers an automatic rollback and a page to your oncall.
[07:09] Markus Lee: we'll prepare the 500 queries — can be anonymized.
[07:14] Rita Gomez: Will also check legal for data residency before we upload.
[07:19] Priya Shah: Great. Next — tuning knobs: we recommend 1) batch size sweep, 2) KV cache warmup prefetch, 3) attention-scaling tweak (we have a parameter we call "attn temp" in the runbook), 4) small learning-free calibration (like per-channel scales) which can reduce drift on FP8.
[07:50] Markus Lee: Can you explain the calibration step? Is that retraining?
[07:55] Priya Shah: It's not full retrain — it's a small calibration pass over a few thousand tokens to fix outlier ranges for quant scaling. Think of it as a micro-statistics pass; some customers run it nightly. We'll include scripts.
[08:14] Jordan Kim: Priya, you added a note about an "attn temp"; is that risky?
[08:19] Priya Shah: It's low risk — it's a multiplier on attention logits pre-softmax to reduce spikeiness caused by reduced precision. Tweaking it 0.95-1.05 can fix some artifacts without touching weights.
[08:36] Tom Alvarez: Who owns the runbook ops? Echelon or Redwood?
[08:41] Jordan Kim: Typically Redwood provides the runbook and scripts; ops can be run by Echelon or by Redwood Dedicated if you choose that model.
[08:50] Rita Gomez: For pilot we want Echelon to run tests but Redwood to run the initial sweep so we can validate the commands.
[08:59] Priya Shah: Sounds good — we'll push a runbook repo and a single command to reproduce the baseline.
[09:12] Jordan Kim: Ok let's move to the anomaly we saw on Wednesday — the p95 spike at ~03:14 in the log. Priya?
[09:20] Priya Shah: Right, that spike correlated with a cold KV cache after a rollout. We saw extra recompute for long contexts, pushing p95 up. The workaround was to prime the cache or route those long contexts to the hosted FP16 for a short window.
[09:42] Markus Lee: Is there a way to pre-prime the cache without actually serving user data?
[09:47] Priya Shah: You can replay a synthetic prefix load that mimics typical conversation turns — that's what we mean by warmup. We can automate that in the runbook.
[09:58] Rita Gomez: sounds reasonable.
[10:03] Jordan Kim: I'm going to share the pilot SOW changes after the call. Tom, any contract questions?
[10:10] Tom Alvarez: Just that we need clarity on rollback SLAs and liability for hallucination-caused incidents. Will review the SOW.
[10:18] Priya Shah: We'll add a section on rollback triggers and an incident review cadence.
[10:24] Jordan Kim: Great. Ok quick live demo — Priya, can you share screen and show the sheet? (screen shared)
[10:40] Priya Shah: Here is the sheet — column A is model variant, B is batch, C is p50 tokens/sec, D p95 latency ms, E error delta vs FP16. See the new INT8 batch=2 run (highlighted). p50 improved by 1.85x but p95 is only marginally better due to cache cold starts.
[11:12] Markus Lee: can you export the run with the raw logs? we'd like to replay.
[11:17] Priya Shah: Yep — raw logs are attached to the sheet; link is in the notes. Also the bench script with exact flags is checked in.
[11:30] Rita Gomez: on the safety front, where do the audit logs live?
[11:35] Priya Shah: Logs go to your S3 if you configure private deployment, or to Redwood audit store for hosted (we can send you the retention options). All entries include token-level metadata for traceability.
[11:50] Tom Alvarez: Any encryption for those logs? KMS?
[11:53] Priya Shah: Yes enterprise keys via KMS, or HSM if you're doing private on-prem.
[12:03] Jordan Kim: Back to quality — Markus, you mentioned some false positives in your evaluation set. Can you share a few?
[12:12] Markus Lee: sent a quick folder to the shared drive — you'll find about 12 flagged examples. We want to prioritize those in the sensitivity sweep.
[12:22] Priya Shah: We'll include those in the 500 validation set. For each we will report a confidence histogram across variants.
[12:32] Jordan Kim: Timeline recap: Priya runs batch sweep and uploads results by 12/10; Markus sends labeled 500 by 12/09; Jordan sends SOW and pricing by 12/08. Any changes?
[12:45] Rita Gomez: we need a short call next week with infra to validate network throughput assumptions. Can we do Wed 12/09 09:00am PST?
[12:55] Jordan Kim: I'll check and tentatively book.
[13:02] Priya Shah: One more technical note — when we do the calibration pass for FP8 we'll also check for per-layer outliers; sometimes a single transformer block causes most of the drift and we can apply per-layer scaling. That often recovers most of the lost accuracy.
[13:24] Markus Lee: good to know. How heavy is the calibration? time-wise?
[13:28] Priya Shah: For our sample it's a few minutes per model on the Aurora-40; negligible compared to full retrain.
[13:36] Tom Alvarez: Ok from budget standpoint can we add a cap on the number of calibration runs in the pilot SOW?
[13:43] Jordan Kim: sure, we'll add a line item with not-to-exceed hours.
[13:50] Rita Gomez: Any thoughts on using a mixed precision blend? We saw a doc about blending layers int8/fp16.
[13:58] Priya Shah: Blend is promising — you can pin sensitive layers to FP16 and others to INT8; it often gives most of the cost savings with minimal quality hit. We'll include a small experimental config for that.
[14:15] Markus Lee: That sounds like a good compromise.
[14:20] Jordan Kim: Alright we're at 40 minutes in — any final questions before we wrap?
[14:27] Tom Alvarez: Please include rollback SLAs + sample incident playbook in the SOW.
[14:32] Jordan Kim: Will do.
[14:36] Priya Shah: I'll queue the reruns and drop a note in the sheet when complete.
[14:40] Rita Gomez: We'll confirm the data upload window — aiming to have the sample set by end of day 12/09.
[14:46] Jordan Kim: Great. Quick recap of next steps on screen... (recap listed).
[14:55] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW.
[15:00] Markus Lee: thanks all.
[15:03] Meeting end.

Post-call quick notes: transcription had a few mislabels (Speaker 3/4 got swapped in earlier auto-export). We saved the bench artifacts in the pilot folder; Priya to attach raw logs and the bench command.
